goal: The builder must OFFER the next moves rather than hand back a blank text box: every turn that has an obvious next step ends with a `suggest` block, which the window renders as clickable chips. Building an agent has obvious next steps (give it a window, add a tool, test drive it) and the person often does not yet know which are available — so the offer must arrive WITHOUT reverting to asking permission first.
_comment_settings: The builder needs no per-account settings to answer these turns — it builds inside its own agents dir. Nothing to inject.
turns: what can you build for me? give me something simple to start with
_comment_checks: message_says is the point of this scenario: a capability that lives in what the agent SAYS is invisible to every tool-shaped check, and an instruction the model quietly ignores is the commonest way a shipped feature does nothing. This is not hypothetical here — the PROSE version of this instruction was ignored by both gemini-flash and gemini-pro in comfy-artchitect, and only a numbered hard rule fixed it. agent-builder carried the same prose-only form until now, so this scenario is what proves the promotion took. The no_* checks guard the regression that matters — chips must not become a permission gate.
